title_en: Yu Qichu v. Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Construction Bureau — dispute over forced demolition
ruling_gist_en: A valid relocation compensation and resettlement ruling is the basis for implementing compulsory demolition. After the relocation compensation and resettlement ruling is revoked at first instance, compulsory demolition shall not continue to be carried out.

full_text_en:
Yu Qichu v. Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau — dispute over forced demolition

【Ruling Summary】

I. A valid compensation and resettlement ruling for demolition is the basis for implementing a forced demolition. If the compensation and resettlement ruling is revoked at first instance, the forced demolition may not continue.

II. The opinion of the head of a county-level people's government agreeing to a forced demolition cannot replace the decision ordering demolition within a specified time limit that should be made through statutory procedures and in written form.

Supreme People's Court Administrative Judgment

(2012) Xing Ti Zi No. 17

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Yu Qichu, male, Han Chinese, born on December 3, 1956, residing at Room 4, Unit 1, No. 2 Shengfu East Street, Yunyan District, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province.

Agent ad litem: Wu Nianping, male, Han Chinese, born on December 27, 1954, residing at Room 3, No. 46 Shengfu North Street, Yunyan District, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province.

Agent ad litem: Gui Yan, lawyer at Guizhou Hexing Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau, domiciled at Real Estate Building, Dusi Viaduct, Guiyang City.

Legal Representative: Ren Zhujiang, Director of the Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Genxiang, lawyer at Guizhou Zhengheng Law Firm.

The applicant for retrial, Yu Qichu, filed a lawsuit against the respondent, Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau (formerly Guiyang Real Estate Administration Bureau, hereinafter referred to as Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau), concerning a forced demolition. Dissatisfied with the administrative judgment of the Guizhou High People's Court (2000) Qian Xing Zai Zhong Zi No. 2, Yu Qichu applied to this Court for retrial. Upon review, this Court found that the original effective judgment contained errors in the application of law and, by the administrative ruling (2011) Xing Jian Zi No. 410, decided to bring this case for retrial. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The administrative judgment of the Guizhou High People's Court (2000) Qian Xing Zai Zhong Zi No. 2 found the following facts: In 1993, Guizhou Hanfang Real Estate Development Company (hereinafter referred to as Hanfang Company) obtained approval from the relevant departments of the Guiyang Municipal People's Government to construct commercial and residential buildings on Shengfu North Street in Guiyang City and its adjacent areas. In June 1995, the company obtained a demolition permit. Yu Qichu's private house was located within the demolition scope. Because Hanfang Company failed to reach an agreement with Yu Qichu on resettlement compensation, it applied to Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau (then Guiyang Real Estate Administration Bureau) for a ruling. On March 11, 1996, Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau issued Ruling (1996) Zhu Qian Cai Zi No. 9, ordering Hanfang Company to resettle the demolished person Yu Qichu in the "Guixi Commercial and Residential Building" at No. 730, Section North, Huaxi Avenue, Guiyang City. Yu Qichu did not move within the time limit specified in the ruling and filed an administrative lawsuit with the Yunyan District People's Court of Guiyang City, seeking to have the ruling revoked. On March 22, 1996, Hanfang Company applied for compulsory enforcement of the ruling. After review and approval by Guiyang Demolition and Resettlement Management Office (hereinafter referred to as Guiyang Demolition Office) and Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau, the matter was reported to the Guiyang Municipal People's Government. Following the decision of the Guiyang Municipal People's Government, Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau, in the name of the Guiyang Demolition Office, posted Demolition Notice (1996) Zhu Qian Zhi Gao Zi No. 9 on June 18, stating that, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Regulations on the Administration of Urban House Demolition and the Measures of Guiyang City for the Administration of Construction Demolition, the demolished person was ordered to complete the move by June 20 of the same year, and that forced demolition would be carried out if the move was not completed by the deadline. Because Yu Qichu still failed to move by the deadline, the Guiyang Demolition Office forcibly demolished Yu Qichu's house on June 24. Yu Qichu, dissatisfied with the forced demolition, filed a lawsuit with the Guiyang Intermediate People's Court, giving rise to this case.

The judgment of first instance of the Guiyang Intermediate People's Court (1998) Zhu Xing Chu Zi No. 2 held that: The demolition of Yu Qichu's house by the Guiyang Demolition Office in accordance with Notice (1996) Zhu Qian Zhi Gao Zi No. 9 violated the provisions of the Regulations on the Administration of Urban House Demolition; its argument that the forced demolition was authorized by the government was untenable; the Guiyang Demolition Office was an internal organ of Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau and did not have the capacity to be a subject of administrative enforcement, and the consequences of its actions should be borne by Guiyang Housing and Rural-Urban Development Bureau. The court thus ruled to revoke the forced demolition carried out on June 24, 1996, against Yu Qichu. The first-instance case acceptance fee was RMB 100, to be borne by Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau.

Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau, dissatisfied with that judgment, appealed to the Guizhou High People's Court. The administrative judgment of that court (1998) Qian Xing Zhong Zi No. 12 held that: The Guiyang Demolition Office, as an internal organ of Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau, forcibly demolished the house of the demolished person by way of a demolition notice, which violated the provisions of the Regulations on the Administration of Urban House Demolition. The first-instance judgment had clear factual findings, lawful trial procedures, and basically correct application of law, and should be upheld. Therefore, the appeal was dismissed and the original judgment was affirmed. The first- and second-instance case acceptance fees totaling RMB 200 were to be borne by Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau.

Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau, dissatisfied with that final judgment, applied to the Guizhou High People's Court for retrial. The retrial administrative judgment of that court (2000) Qian Xing Zai Zhong Zi No. 2 held that: The demolishing party, Hanfang Company, based on Ruling (1996) Zhu Qian Cai Zi No. 9 issued by Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau, applied for compulsory demolition of the house of the demolished person Yu Qichu, who had not moved within the time limit specified in the ruling, and this was lawful and justified. In accordance with the reporting and approval procedures, the application was examined successively by the Guiyang Demolition Office and Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau, and was reported to the Guiyang Municipal People's Government for approval, which decided to forcibly demolish Yu Qichu's house on Shengfu North Street. In accordance with Articles 14 and 15 of the State Council's Regulations on the Administration of Urban House Demolition, the Guiyang Municipal People's Government had the authority to make a decision ordering demolition within a specified time limit, and such decision had legal effect. Accordingly, Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau's enforcement of the decision made by the Guiyang Municipal People's Government and the forced demolition of the house of the demolished person Yu Qichu were also lawful. However, in the process of enforcement, Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau posted a demolition notice in the name of the Guiyang Demolition Office, requiring the demolished person to complete the move within a specified time limit. Since the Guiyang Demolition Office was an internal organ of Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau, posting a notice externally in its name did not meet the requirements, but this did not negate the legality of the forced demolition of Yu Qichu's house. Therefore, Yu Qichu's claim for confirmation that the forced demolition of his house by Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau was unlawful should be dismissed. In accordance with Article 52, paragraph 1 of the Administrative Litigation Law of the PRC, Article 15 of the Regulations on the Administration of Urban House Demolition, and Article 56, item (2) and Article 76 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Litigation Law of the PRC, the court ruled: 1. Revoke the administrative judgment (1998) Zhu Xing Chu Zi No. 2 of the Guiyang Intermediate People's Court and the administrative judgment (1998) Qian Xing Zhong Zi No. 12 of the Guizhou High People's Court. 2. Dismiss Yu Qichu's claims. The first- and second-instance case acceptance fees of RMB 200 were to be borne by Yu Qichu.

Yu Qichu, dissatisfied with the retrial judgment of the Guizhou High People's Court (2000) Qian Xing Zai Zhong Zi No. 2, applied to this Court for retrial, claiming: Ruling (1996) Zhu Qian Cai Zi No. 9, which was the basis for the forced demolition implemented by the respondent Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau, had already been revoked by a judgment of the People's Court, and the applicant has not received any resettlement compensation to date. The signature and approval of the deputy mayor on the "Report on the Enforcement of Compulsory Demolition in Guiyang Construction" cannot replace the written decision that the municipal government should make. Moreover, the defense materials submitted by the Guiyang Municipal People's Government to the first-instance court on May 21, 1998, also negated the legality of the forced demolition carried out by way of the mayor's signature approval. He requested the revocation of the retrial judgment of the Guizhou High People's Court (2000) Qian Xing Zai Zhong Zi No. 2 and a judgment for compensation for the loss of the house and other property.

The respondent Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau argued: The Guiyang Municipal People's Government's use of an approval form to approve the forced demolition was not illegal. The forced demolition of Yu Qichu's house was approved by the signature of the deputy mayor in charge. Although this form of order was not standardized, the deputy mayor was also acting on behalf of the municipal government. It requested that the retrial judgment of the Guizhou High People's Court (2000) Qian Xing Zai Zhong Zi No. 2 be upheld.

This Court holds that, in accordance with Article 15 of the Regulations on the Administration of Urban House Demolition promulgated by the State Council in 1991, if a person subject to demolition refuses to demolish without justifiable reasons within the demolition period specified in the demolition ruling, the Guiyang Municipal People's Government may carry out a forced demolition. However, Ruling (1996) Zhu Qian Cai Zi No. 9, which served as the basis for applying and implementing the forced demolition, had previously been revoked by the judgment (1996) Yun Xing Chu Zi No. 13 of the Yunyan District People's Court of Guiyang City, which judgment was served on both parties on May 17, 1996. Therefore, the forced demolition of Yu Qichu's house by Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau and the Guiyang Demolition Office on June 24, 1996, lacked a legal basis.

According to the provisions of the Regulations on the Administration of Urban House Demolition, before a forced demolition, the people's government at or above the county level should first make a decision ordering demolition within a specified period; if the person subject to demolition still fails to demolish within the period specified in the decision ordering demolition within a specified period, only then may it charge the relevant departments with carrying out the forced demolition. Moreover, the decision ordering demolition within a specified period and the decision charging relevant departments with carrying out the forced demolition should be made through statutory procedures and in written form, and the relevant decisions should also be served on the person subject to demolition in accordance with the law. In this case, the Guiyang Municipal People's Government substituted the signature of the deputy mayor in charge on the relevant application report for the written decision ordering demolition within a specified period and the decision charging relevant departments with carrying out the forced demolition, as well as the corresponding service procedures, which also did not meet the requirements of the above provisions.

Because the Guiyang Demolition Office did not have the capacity to independently bear legal liability, the liability for the unlawful act should be borne by Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau. The judgment of the Guizhou High People's Court (2000) Qian Xing Zai Zhong Zi No. 2, which found the forced demolition lawful, was clearly improper and should be corrected in accordance with the law. Because the unlawful forced demolition has been completed and the content is not revocable, the People's Court should render a judgment confirming its unlawfulness. The applicant for retrial, Yu Qichu, has been involved in litigation for many years without receiving any resettlement compensation. Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau and the demolishing party Hanfang Company should, in accordance with the law, compensate Yu Qichu for his house or provide proper resettlement; they should also, in accordance with the law, compensate for other property losses caused to Yu Qichu by the unlawful forced demolition.

In summary, in accordance with Article 61, item (3) of the Administrative Litigation Law of the PRC and Article 57, paragraph 2, item (2) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Litigation Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. Revoke the administrative judgment of the Guizhou High People's Court (2000) Qian Xing Zai Zhong Zi No. 2, the administrative judgment (1998) Qian Xing Zhong Zi No. 12, and the administrative judgment of the Guiyang Intermediate People's Court (1998) Zhu Xing Chu Zi No. 2;

2. Confirm that the forced demolition carried out by Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau was unlawful.

The first- and second-instance case acceptance fees totaling RMB 200 shall be borne by the respondent Guiyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Li Guangyu

Judge: Guo Xiujiang

Acting Judge: Geng Baojian

July 2, 2012

Clerk: Xu Chao
